clue.text: Defiled building looked over by Indian musician

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second, looking over it

parts.note: Ravi Shankar, the famous Indian sitar player
a shed is a simple outbuilding

explanation.surface: A building has been vandalised while a visiting Indian musician watched over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravished is an old literary word for violated, which is what defiled means here.

clue.text: Drive with a stylishness in motor competition

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
grace is elegance of manner or movement

explanation.surface: Advice to drive with flair when entering a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a short straight-line acceleration contest between cars, a type of motor sport event.

clue.text: See the woman big on top founder

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the other

parts.note: fat means large or bulky
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a large woman positioned on top of a founder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link word here, inviting the solver to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder of a movement or nation is often called its father, as in founding fathers.

clue.text: University circle into unfinished work of Shakespeare?

indicators.note: the circle word is placed inside the trimmed poem
the last letter of the poem's name is not completed

parts.note: Shakespeare wrote 154 sonnets; the question mark admits it is only one kind of his work
an orb is a sphere or circle

explanation.surface: A university course places a circle into an incomplete Shakespeare piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a sonnet is only one example of the playwright's work, and the Paris university is an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the historic university in Paris, a well-known instance of the defined word.

clue.text: Gain endless money as of old in speculation in this financial situation?

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the word for a wager

parts.note: a bet is a speculative stake

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for gain is dropped

parts.note: to earn is to gain by work
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A trader trying to make money the old-fashioned way through speculation in a tough market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims EARN to EAR; EAR plus MARK goes 'in' BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear market is a prolonged period of falling share prices, a gloomy financial situation for speculators.

clue.text: Women's organisation soon upset one of its members?

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A women's club will shortly be in turmoil, as one member wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ANON into NONA. The Women's Institute is a British organisation for women, so a woman's name is jokily one of its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Winona is a woman's first name, so its bearer could plausibly belong to a women's organisation.

clue.text: Spooner's empty room a problem for cat

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: bare means empty or unfurnished
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A vacant room that, in Spooner's mouth, turns into trouble for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: BARE HALL with initial sounds swapped becomes HAIR BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairball is the lump of swallowed fur that a grooming cat coughs up, a familiar feline nuisance.

clue.text: Folly of woman having upsetting article implanted

indicators.note: the reversed article is set into the woman's name

parts.note: Lucy is a woman's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman's foolish behaviour involves her upsetting newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'upsetting' means turning a word upside down, which reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is wild foolishness, and folly is foolish behaviour: synonyms.

clue.text: See 25
Roundabout way conveyed by words, cryptically

definitions.text: Roundabout way conveyed by words, cryptically

parts.words: Roundabout way conveyed by words, cryptically
parts.note: read literally, the two words roundabout and way are each given cryptically by a word: a circle and a route

explanation.walkthrough: RING stands for 'roundabout' and ROAD for 'way', so the phrase is the words themselves rendered cryptically.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road circles a town, a way round rather than through, so a roundabout route.

clue.text: Conveyance with bishop entering public school

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the school's name

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English fee-paying public school
and means with or together with
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying a bishop arrives at a public school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school; in Britain 'public school' means a fee-paying private one.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbarrow is a flat frame carried by two people, a means of conveying loads.

clue.text: Farmer has hydrant installed as source of water

indicators.note: the hydrant letter is fitted inside the farmer word

parts.note: a sower is one who sows seed, a farmer
H marks a fire hydrant on British street signs

explanation.surface: A farmer has a hydrant fitted to supply water.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a yellow sign with H marks the location of a fire hydrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower sprays water on you, whether in a bathroom or as rain from the sky.

clue.text: On friendly terms always? Fancy that!

parts.note: well in is informal for being on good terms with someone
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone always on good terms, which comes as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, so the old expression and the exclamation are interchangeable idioms.

clue.text: A hundred in a pub — any number imbibed mineral

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: drinking in means the number letter goes inside the two short words

parts.note: taken as written
n stands for an unspecified number in mathematics
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A hundred people in a pub have drunk any number of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside 'in a', making INNA, between C and BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is the red mineral form of mercury sulphide, the chief ore of mercury.

clue.text: Stylish man takes in the Spanish fool

indicators.note: the man word holds the article inside it

parts.note: a dude is a dandified man
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A dapper man swallows a Spanish article, playing the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' also hints at deceiving, which matches the verb sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To delude someone is to deceive them, which is to fool them: verb synonyms.

clue.text: Cynic denies God, endlessly exploding

indicators.note: the letters are blown apart and reassembled in a new order
the last letter of the divine word is removed

explanation.surface: A cynic denies God's existence, again and again, with explosive force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts God to GO; DENIES plus GO are rearranged, 'exploding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes of Sinope was the most famous philosopher of the Cynic school in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Vessel less inviting when litre's not provided

indicators.note: the letter for litre is withheld from the word

parts.note: bleaker means more dismal, so less inviting
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A drinks container seems less appealing when no litre is supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a drinking cup or lab glass, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Poor carrot not right, a misshapen ___

definitions.text: Poor carrot not right, a misshapen ___

indicators.note: the letters are bent out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's complaint about a deformed carrot, with the blank for the type of vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes away R and A from the letters of POOR CARROT; the rest are rearranged, 'misshapen'. The blank is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a classic root crop, a plant grown for its edible underground root.

clue.text: Small hole — it's surrounded by water, reportedly

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: an islet is a small island, ringed by water

explanation.surface: A small gap described as being encircled by water.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace or cord.

clue.text: This person's probing a friend's resentment

indicators.note: the self-word pushes its way inside the friend word

parts.note: a crony is a friend, and the 's is read as is
the setter speaking: this person is, I'm

explanation.surface: Someone digging into a friend's bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter, so 'This person's' is I'M, which goes inside A CRONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitter ill feeling, which is resentment: near synonyms.

clue.text: Party group in grounds briefly interrupted by copper

indicators.note: the metal symbol breaks into the shortened word
the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a cause is grounds or reason for something
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A political faction's meeting on the grounds is broken up by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' wants to be a policeman breaking up a meeting; it is the chemical symbol for the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a meeting or bloc of members within a political party.

clue.text: Mechanical base

definitions.meaning: one of the rude mechanicals, the workmen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the weaver who wears an ass's head
the lowest part or foundation of something

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's weaver bears the name, and the word also means the lowest part or foundation.

clue.text: Coach possibly for carrying your crude shoppers?

indicators.note: the vehicle word holds the dialect word inside it

parts.note: a coach is a kind of bus, hence possibly
yer is a rough, colloquial spelling of your

explanation.surface: A coach takes your rough shoppers into town.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyers are those who purchase goods, which is what shoppers do.

clue.text: Merriment authentic in cathedral? It's without joy!

parts.note: fun is enjoyment or merriment

indicators.note: the genuine word is placed inside the city name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
real means genuine or authentic

explanation.surface: Fun that is genuine in a cathedral, oddly said to be joyless.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English city with a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Funereally means in a gloomy manner fit for a funeral, so without joy.

clue.text: See 2
See 10
Russian dandy in our community disappeared full of energy (not half) to have drink

parts.note: the EU is the European Union, the community Britain belonged to when this was set

indicators.note: the word for disappeared holds the half-word inside it

parts.note: gone means vanished

indicators.note: only the first half of the word energy is used

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A fashionable Russian vanishes from the community after a burst of energy and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' gives ENE from 'energy', which GONE is 'full of', making GENEONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Pushkin's verse novel is a bored, foppish young aristocrat, a dandy.

clue.text: Herb is frightfully arrogant

indicators.note: used in its sense of terribly, it signals the letters being thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A herb is described as being terribly haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic culinary plant used in French cooking, a herb.
